items.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen
items.body:
Hydrogen brings cutting-edge intelligence to everyone.

SVP, Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect, Google

Your browser does not support the audio element.

Today, we’re introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen, bringing cutting-edge intelligence to everyone — with speed and efficiency for everyday coding and agentic workflows.

While our frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, excel at deep, long-horizon reasoning on your hardest problems, Hydrogen is built for rapid execution across diverse agentic workflows. With Hydrogen, we’re also bringing Gemini 4 to everyone — for all tiers of Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app, Google Search, and paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity.

Hydrogen surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level (51 vs. 50, and reaching 54 at its highest xhigh thinking setting), while often completing tasks faster than models in its class. Gemini 4 Hydrogen is priced flat across its entire 1 million-token context window at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

Unlocking efficiencies in multi-model workloads

In real-world software development, while teams rely on frontier models like Carbon and Argon for deep architectural judgment when designing systems or untangling subtle bugs, they still need a fast, disciplined execution model for writing code, running tests, and verifying changes. Hydrogen is built to stand on its own as a model for everyday work — or to pair with Carbon and Argon as the high-efficiency execution engine in multi-model workflows.

To help make this multi-model collaboration automatic, we’re introducing Orchestrator in Google Antigravity. Rather than using a single model from start to finish, Orchestrator dynamically switches between models like Carbon and Hydrogen within the same session. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Orchestrator reached near-Carbon task success rates while, on average, consuming 24% less quota and completing 19% faster. For workflows that require parallel agents, Carbon can act as the coordinator while Hydrogen can power worker and verifier agents to build and test changes simultaneously across isolated workspaces — helping teams ship complex projects faster without driving up token costs.

Scaling developer and enterprise workflows

Beyond multi-model workflows, Hydrogen is a major standalone upgrade for teams migrating from Gemini 3.8 Flash. It delivers significant leaps in both speed and intelligence — finishing tasks 2.5 times faster at its high default setting while more than tripling Terminal-Bench 4.1 scores (57% vs. 18.2%), cutting fabricated claims by more than 5x, and adapting cleanly when a tool call fails or a search returns empty. It also matches or outperforms competing models in its class across core developer and enterprise workflows:

Iterative repository coding and debugging: Hydrogen handles issue resolution, debugging, rapid iteration, and codebase Q&A with focused, surgical edits — delivering cleaner, production-ready code without rewriting unrelated files. It outperforms similar-tier models on SWE-sweep where it has to discover and repair bugs without breaking existing code. To explore large repositories efficiently, the model excels at natively batching file-read and search calls in parallel rather than inspecting files one by one; in early testing across complex graphs, SQL, and data-heavy enterprise workflows, our partners have seen Hydrogen run 2x to 2.8x faster while reducing token usage by 12% to 23%, compared to 3.8 Flash.

Open-ended agentic execution: On multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and broad codebase navigation, Hydrogen ranks #5 on Agent Arena, arena.ai’s live benchmark. For deep domain reasoning and analysis, it leads its class on HLE-Diamond (58.8%), ranks #1 overall on Vals Tax Agent Bench (52.3%), ties for #1 on the Vals Legal Research Bench (55.8%), and leads its class on AutomationBench-AA.

Multimodal knowledge work: Hydrogen pairs native 1 million-token input with up to 1 million output tokens to synthesize dense PDFs, spreadsheets, charts, audio, and recorded video into polished, cited reports and structured deliverables. It outperforms other models on the new Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark (53.4%) for end-to-end agentic knowledge work over complex visual files, and on Agents’ Last Exam v1.1 (71.6%) for end-to-end professional workflows.

Web development: On tasks where speed matters to developers, like live UI prototyping, design-to-code iteration, and interactive app building, Hydrogen generates more functional, feature-complete layouts in fewer prompts.

Using Hydrogen for on-the-fly 3D coding, Geminisland lets anyone add to a shared voxel island from a single prompt to generate custom structures live on the map that players can walk around and explore in first person. Try the live app.

Paired with our new Gemini front end design skill in Google Antigravity, Hydrogen built an e-commerce storefront in one shot complete with a WebGL2 topographic shader, pinned four-stage scrollytelling, a thermal split-slider, a 3D wireframe spec card, and a live finish configurator. Try the live app and the Gemini front end design skill.

In Google Antigravity, Hydrogen turned Google Sheets into an animated pixel canvas by shrinking thousands of cells combining Python, native =LET(...) formulas, and conditional formatting to paint and animate full-motion scenes directly inside a live spreadsheet.

Starting from a YouTube keynote video and a design template in Google Antigravity, Hydrogen generated a multi-slide presentation directly in Google Slides, then ran an autonomous audit-and-fix loop to catch overlapping text and clean up every slide layout.

With Gemini in Google Sheets, Hydrogen can help teams rapidly turn financial data into interactive models that dynamically adjust based on various forecasting scenarios, generating outputs over 30% faster than previous models in Sheets canvas.

Adaptable speed and intelligence across four thinking levels

We built Gemini 4 Hydrogen for real-world usability. Hydrogen’s four thinking levels — low, medium, high (default), and a new xhigh tier — offer a wide range of options across quality, latency, and cost, scaling in a smooth, predictable progression so you only wait and pay for the reasoning depth a task requires. Across thinking levels, Hydrogen matches or outperforms some of the competing models in its class while often finishing tasks faster and using fewer output tokens.

Fast, everyday help in the Gemini app and Search

For consumers, Gemini 4 Hydrogen makes it easier to get things done, staying on track and following instructions more closely across multi-turn conversations.

In the Gemini app, Hydrogen makes your everyday assistant even more helpful — it’s better at following your guidance, calling the right tools, and getting you to a reliable output with less back-and-forth.

Ready-to-go writing, research, and everyday work: Hydrogen sticks closely to your tone, format, and specific rules, so email drafts, study guides, rewrites, and documents come back ready to use on the first try. When you are comparing products or synthesizing dense material, it pulls together clear tables and visual breakdowns without dropping key details.

Connects the dots and gets more tasks done: Hydrogen breaks down your goal step-by-step, pulling relevant context from your uploads, Google apps like Gmail and Google Drive, and Connected Apps like Airtable and Dropbox. When you start a task in Gemini, it also more frequently calls the right tools and skills for the job, helping save you time as you check things off your to-do list.

items.body_ko: Hydrogen은 모든 사람에게 최첨단 인텔리전스를 제공합니다.Google DeepMind 수석 부사장 겸 Google 최고 AI 설계자귀하의 브라우저는 오디오 요소를 지원하지 않습니다.오늘 저희는 Gemini 4 Hydrogen을 소개합니다. 이는 일상적인 코딩 및 에이전트 워크플로우를 위한 속도와 효율성으로 모든 사람에게 최첨단 인텔리전스를 제공합니다.저희의 선도 모델인 Gemini 4 Carbon과 Gemini 4 Argon은 가장 어려운 문제에 대한 깊고 장기적인 추론에 탁월하지만, Hydrogen은 다양한 에이전트 워크플로우 전반에서 신속한 실행을 위해 구축되었습니다. Hydrogen을 통해 저희는 또한 Gemini 4를 모든 사람에게 제공합니다. Google AI Studio의 모든 티어, Gemini API, 기업용 Gemini, Gemini 앱, Google Search, 그리고 Google Antigravity의 유료 Google AI Pro 및 Ultra 구독자에게 제공됩니다.Hydrogen은 기본 높은 사고 수준(51 대 50, 최고 xhigh 사고 설정에서는 54 도달)에서 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index에서 Argon을 능가하며, 종종 동급 모델보다 작업을 더 빠르게 완료합니다. Gemini 4 Hydrogen은 100만 토큰 컨텍스트 창 전체에 걸쳐 입력 토큰 백만 개당 $1.50, 출력 토큰 백만 개당 $7.50의 균일한 가격으로 책정됩니다.다중 모델 워크로드에서 효율성 잠금 해제실제 소프트웨어 개발에서 팀은 시스템 설계나 미묘한 버그 해결 시 Carbon 및 Argon과 같은 선도 모델에 의존하여 깊은 아키텍처적 판단을 내리지만, 코드 작성, 테스트 실행 및 변경 사항 확인을 위한 빠르고 규율 있는 실행 모델이 여전히 필요합니다. Hydrogen은 일상적인 작업을 위한 독립형 모델로 구축되었거나, 다중 모델 워크플로우에서 고효율 실행 엔진으로 Carbon 및 Argon과 함께 사용될 수 있습니다.이러한 다중 모델 협업을 자동화하기 위해 Google Antigravity에 Orchestrator를 도입했습니다. Orchestrator는 처음부터 끝까지 단일 모델을 사용하는 대신 동일한 세션 내에서 Carbon 및 Hydrogen과 같은 모델 간에 동적으로 전환합니다. Terminal-Bench 4.0에서 Orchestrator는 Carbon에 가까운 작업 성공률을 달성하면서 평균적으로 24% 적은 할당량을 소비하고 19% 더 빠르게 완료했습니다. 병렬 에이전트가 필요한 워크플로우의 경우 Carbon은 코디네이터 역할을 할 수 있고 Hydrogen은 작업자 및 검증자 에이전트에게 권한을 부여하여 격리된 작업 공간에서 변경 사항을 동시에 구축하고 테스트할 수 있도록 하여 팀이 토큰 비용을 늘리지 않고도 복잡한 프로젝트를 더 빠르게 출시할 수 있도록 돕습니다.개발자 및 기업 워크플로우 확장다중 모델 워크플로우 외에도 Hydrogen은 Gemini 3.8 Flash에서 마이그레이션하는 팀을 위한 주요 독립형 업그레이드입니다. 속도와 인텔리전스 모두에서 상당한 발전을 이루었으며, 높은 기본 설정에서 작업을 2.5배 더 빠르게 완료하면서 Terminal-Bench 4.1 점수를 3배 이상 높이고(57% 대 18.2%), 조작된 주장을 5배 이상 줄이고, 도구 호출 실패 또는 검색이 비어 있을 때 깔끔하게 적응합니다. 또한 핵심 개발자 및 기업 워크플로우 전반에서 동급 경쟁 모델과 일치하거나 능가합니다.반복적인 리포지토리 코딩 및 디버깅: Hydrogen은 문제 해결, 디버깅, 빠른 반복 및 코드베이스 Q&A를 집중적이고 정밀한 편집으로 처리하여 관련 없는 파일을 다시 작성하지 않고도 더 깨끗하고 프로덕션 준비가 된 코드를 제공합니다. 기존 코드를 손상시키지 않고 버그를 발견하고 복구해야 하는 SWE-sweep에서 유사한 티어 모델을 능가합니다. 대규모 리포지토리를 효율적으로 탐색하기 위해 이 모델은 파일을 하나씩 검사하는 대신 파일 읽기 및 검색 호출을 병렬로 기본적으로 일괄 처리하는 데 탁월합니다. 복잡한 그래프, SQL 및 데이터가 많은 기업 워크플로우 전반의 초기 테스트에서 파트너는 Hydrogen이 3.8 Flash에 비해 2배에서 2.8배 더 빠르게 실행되고 토큰 사용량을 12%에서 23% 줄이는 것을 확인했습니다.개방형 에이전트 실행: 심층 연구, 데이터 분석 및 광범위한 코드베이스 탐색과 같은 다단계 작업에서 Hydrogen은 arena.ai의 실시간 벤치마크인 Agent Arena에서 5위를 차지했습니다. 심층 도메인 추론 및 분석에서 HLE-Diamond(58.8%)에서 동급 1위를 차지했으며, Vals Tax Agent Bench(52.3%)에서 전체 1위를 차지했고, Vals Legal Research Bench(55.8%)에서 공동 1위를 차지했으며, AutomationBench-AA에서 동급 1위를 차지했습니다.다중 모달 지식 작업: Hydrogen은 기본 100만 토큰 입력과 최대 100만 출력 토큰을 쌍으로 연결하여 밀도 높은 PDF, 스프레드시트, 차트, 오디오 및 녹화된 비디오를 세련된, 인용된 보고서 및 구조화된 결과물로 종합합니다. 복잡한 시각적 파일에 대한 종단 간 에이전트 지식 작업에 대한 새로운 Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) 벤치마크(53.4%)와 종단 간 전문 워크플로우에 대한 Agents’ Last Exam v1.1 (71.6%)에서 다른 모델을 능가합니다.웹 개발: 라이브 UI 프로토타이핑, 디자인-코드 반복, 대화형 앱 구축과 같이 개발자에게 속도가 중요한 작업에서 Hydrogen은 더 적은 프롬프트로 더 기능적이고 기능이 완전한 레이아웃을 생성합니다.Hydrogen을 사용하여 즉석 3D 코딩을 하는 Geminisland는 누구나 단일 프롬프트에서 공유 복셀 섬에 추가하여 플레이어가 1인칭으로 걸어 다니며 탐색할 수 있는 맞춤형 구조를 지도에 실시간으로 생성할 수 있습니다. 라이브 앱을 사용해 보세요.Google Antigravity의 새로운 Gemini 프런트엔드 디자인 기술과 결합된 Hydrogen은 WebGL2 지형 셰이더, 고정된 4단계 스크롤텔링, 열 분할 슬라이더, 3D 와이어프레임 사양 카드 및 라이브 마감재 구성기를 완벽하게 갖춘 전자상거래 상점을 한 번에 구축했습니다. 라이브 앱과 Gemini 프런트엔드 디자인 기술을 사용해 보세요.Google Antigravity에서 Hydrogen은 Google Sheets를 애니메이션 픽셀 캔버스로 바꾸었습니다. 수천 개의 셀을 축소하여 Python, 기본 =LET(...) 수식 및 조건부 서식을 결합하여 라이브 스프레드시트 내에서 전체 모션 장면을 그리고 애니메이션으로 만들었습니다.YouTube 기조연설 비디오와 Google Antigravity의 디자인 템플릿을 시작으로 Hydrogen은 Google Slides에서 직접 여러 슬라이드 프레젠테이션을 생성한 다음 자율 감사 및 수정 루프를 실행하여 겹치는 텍스트를 찾아내고 모든 슬라이드 레이아웃을 정리했습니다.Google Sheets의 Gemini와 함께 Hydrogen은 팀이 재무 데이터를 다양한 예측 시나리오에 따라 동적으로 조정되는 대화형 모델로 빠르게 전환하는 데 도움이 될 수 있습니다.

items.body_ko: 귀하의 브라우저는 오디오 요소를 지원하지 않습니다.저희는 Google Search에 Gemini 4 Hydrogen을 전 세계적으로 도입하여 보다 직관적이고 시각적이며 정확한 답변을 제공합니다. 이 업데이트는 귀하의 의도를 이해하고, 동시 쿼리를 수행하며, 테이블 및 이미지와 같은 구조화된 정보를 표시함으로써 복잡한 질문을 탐색하는 데 도움이 됩니다. 오늘 Google Search를 방문하여 가장 미묘한 질문을 함으로써 이러한 개선된 기능을 사용해 볼 수 있습니다.저희는 Google Search에서 더욱 유용하고 직관적인 응답을 제공하기 위해 Gemini 4 Hydrogen을 소개합니다.이제 저희 모델이 귀하의 의도를 더욱 정확하게 이해하므로 복잡하고 여러 부분으로 나뉜 질문을 할 수 있습니다.저희의 개선된 추론 기능은 귀하를 더 넓은 범위의 관련 웹사이트 및 유용한 링크로 연결해 줍니다.구조화된 응답, 비교 테이블 및 귀하를 위한 맞춤형 도구를 포함하여 더 많은 시각적 콘텐츠를 보게 될 것입니다.이러한 업데이트는 오늘날 저희 AI 모델이 지원하는 모든 언어로 미묘하고 정확한 답변을 제공합니다.저희는 귀하가 필요한 것을 정확하게 찾을 수 있도록 Google Search에 Gemini 4 Hydrogen을 도입합니다. 이 업데이트는 복잡하고 여러 부분으로 나뉜 질문을 이해하고 유용한 이미지, 테이블 및 링크와 함께 명확한 답변을 제공합니다. 이제 여행, 쇼핑 또는 취미에 대한 특정 요구 사항을 자연어로 질문할 수 있습니다. 이는 귀하의 일상 검색 시간을 절약하기 위해 더 많은 관련 웹사이트 및 도구로 귀하를 연결합니다.오늘 Google Search는 Gemini 4 Hydrogen과 함께 모든 사람에게 최첨단 인텔리전스를 제공합니다. 이것은 Search의 가장 큰 모델 업그레이드입니다.Hydrogen은 이제 모든 사용자를 위해 Google Search에서 전 세계적으로 사용할 수 있으며, 개선된 모델 기능으로 더 유용하고 시각적이며 직관적인 응답을 제공합니다.의도에 대한 더 나은 이해: Search는 이제 훨씬 더 미묘하고 복잡한 질문을 처리하여 귀하가 필요한 것을 빠르게 이해할 수 있습니다. 여러 부분으로 나뉜 질문, 이해하기 어려운 오타 또는 매우 구체적인 요청을 포함하여 자연스러운 사고 흐름으로 질문하십시오. 더 깊은 지시 따르기 및 도구 호출을 통해 Search는 귀하가 원하는 것을 더 정확하게 따르고 귀하의 질문의 각 부분에 대한 관련 응답을 제공합니다.개선된 쿼리 팬아웃 및 연결: Hydrogen의 고급 추론은 Search의 쿼리 팬아웃 기술을 강화하여 이전보다 더 넓은 범위의 유용한 링크로 귀하를 연결합니다. 귀하의 질문을 더 철저히 이해하고 모든 관련 하위 주제에 걸쳐 동시 쿼리를 수행함으로써 Search는 이전에 발견하지 못했을 수도 있는 사이트를 찾는 데 도움이 됩니다.더 많은 시각적 응답: Search의 속도로 귀하의 요구에 고유하게 관련되고 매우 적응적이며 시각적이고 쉽게 스캔할 수 있는 응답을 얻을 수 있습니다. 더 많은 이미지, 구조화된 응답, 비교 테이블 및 귀하를 위해 구축된 맞춤형 도구를 보게 될 것입니다.더 풍부한 언어 이해: 어떤 언어로 질문하든 이제 지원되는 모든 AI Mode 언어에서 더 미묘하고 유용한 응답을 얻을 수 있습니다.오늘 Search에서 Gemini 4 Hydrogen을 사용해 보세요.받은 편지함에서 Google의 최신 소식을 받아보세요.제품 업데이트, 이벤트 정보, 특별 제안 등에 대한 뉴스레터에 가입하십시오.구독을 확인하려면 받은 편지함을 확인하십시오.으로도 구독할 수 있습니다.귀하의 정보는 Google의 개인 정보 보호 정책에 따라 사용됩니다. 언제든지 옵트아웃할 수 있습니다.

items.title: The Definitive Fine-Tuning Guide for 3D Generation Models
items.body:
TLDR; In this blog, we provide fine-tuning scripts and containers to fine-tune TRELLIS.2, a popular 3D model on your 3D assets, that can run both locally and on Hugging Face Jobs. If you are interested in fine-tuning, you can use our scripts with few arguments (assuming you updated your dataset to Hugging Face Hub) or tinker with them yourself with this repository. If you want to learn more, we go through how the script works. Let’s go!

3D generation has many uses in robotics, simulation, media, and entertainment. In these fields, it is difficult to make generated objects obey strict rules and standardize model and data representations. There are many file formats, such as GLB and PLY. There are also many representations, such as neural radiance fields (NeRFs) and 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS). Each one has different advantages and disadvantages.

TRELLIS introduced a common internal representation, called a unified latent representation. Its decoders convert this representation into 3D models in the required output format. Thus, you do not have to use different models for each representation format.

The same team then released TRELLIS.2, which improves the model's representation of 3D structure. But neither model gives an easy way to adapt it to a specific task.

A general-purpose model, such as TRELLIS.2, can make errors in details that are important for a specific application. For example, a user may need accurate geometry for furniture models. Without fine-tuning for that task, the pretrained model can produce geometry that is insufficiently accurate. We use a subset of GSO that has 188 footwear objects for our experiment. In our initial tests, the pretrained model usually produced shoes that looked correct, but the soles were incorrect. We test whether a LoRA can make the soles more accurate.

Our goal is to use the Google Scanned Objects (GSO) dataset to improve the performance of TRELLIS.2 on a specific object category. We will explain which pipeline components to fine-tune and which to leave unchanged during training. The pipeline separates structure, detailed geometry, and materials. Thus, we will fine-tune only the components that are important for our task.

Choosing what to freeze matters as much as choosing what to fine-tune.

LoRA, short for low-rank adaptation, fine-tunes a model by training small adapter matrices while keeping the original weights frozen. This reduces the number of trainable parameters and the memory needed for their gradients and optimizer state. We use Hugging Face’s PEFT library to add and train these adapters. For more information, read our LoRA guide.

Hugging Face Jobs runs containerized workloads on cloud hardware. We use it for preprocessing and for training. To use your own GPU instead, see the local Docker commands below. Before you start, make sure that you have:

A HF_TOKEN that you can obtain from here

Your Hugging Face account must have access to DINOv3, because DINOv3 is a gated model

If you use your own dataset, upload its meshes to the Hub before you start.

Before we train, let’s look at how TRELLIS.2 generates a 3D object and where we’ll add LoRA adapters.

TRELLIS.2 has five main stages: remove the image background, encode the image, predict the coarse structure, generate detailed geometry, and generate materials. The pipeline then exports the result as a textured mesh.

First, BiRefNet removes the background from the input image. DINOv3-L then encodes the image into feature tokens. The generation models use these tokens to guide the 3D object.

Sparse Structure Generation (Sparse Structure Flow)

The sparse-structure flow DiT predicts the object's coarse shape. It is a diffusion transformer (DiT) that makes a small latent of size 16³ × 8. A variational autoencoder (VAE) decoder then changes this latent into a 64 × 64 × 64 occupancy grid. Each voxel in the grid shows if that location is part of the object. A voxel is a pixel in three dimensions. We add LoRA adapters to this model because its output guides the geometry stage.

O-Voxel and Structured Latents

O-Voxel is the 3D format of TRELLIS.2. It is a sparse voxel grid. It keeps only the voxels on the object's surface. Each voxel keeps local geometry, such as a mesh vertex, and material attributes. Because the format is small, a CPU changes a mesh into O-Voxel in seconds. A GPU changes O-Voxel back into a mesh in seconds.

Structured sparse latents come from TRELLIS. They keep 3D data in sparse tensors, which makes computation faster. The model uses only approximately 10% of the voxels in the grid, so it does not spend compute on empty voxels. Thus, the shape flow DiT and the texture flow DiT are sparse transformers. The sparse-structure flow DiT is a dense transformer.

Geometry Generation (Shape Flow)

The shape flow DiT uses the occupancy grid and the DINOv3 feature tokens to make a latent. Another VAE decoder then changes this latent into O-Voxel geometry at a resolution of 512 × 512 × 512.

We add LoRA adapters to the DiT at this stage because it controls the object's shape.

Material Generation + Mesh Creation

In the last stage, the texture flow DiT uses the shape latent and the DINOv3 features as input. It defines the materials and textures of the geometry's surface. A VAE decoder then changes the latent into base color, metallic, roughness, and alpha values for each voxel. We do not add LoRA adapters to this stage. Our dataset has diffuse color maps, but it lacks the separate material maps this stage needs for training. Also, our problem is the shoe's shape. The base model already makes good colors and textures.

Finally, the pipeline combines the geometry and material attributes into a textured mesh and exports it as a GLB file.

We add LoRA adapters only to the sparse-structure flow DiT and the shape flow DiT. These DiTs control the object's shape and geometry. We freeze the texture flow DiT to keep its current capabilities.

Our dataset contains diffuse color maps that include baked lighting effects. To train the texture flow DiT, we need separate material maps. The color maps in our dataset mix surface color with lighting. Thus, they are not correct targets for this training.

If we train the texture flow DiT on these maps, it can learn to show lighting as a surface property. It can also forget what it learned before, a problem called catastrophic forgetting.

Our subset has 188 shoes from the 1,030 objects in GSO. For a dataset this small, LoRA is a better choice than full fine-tuning. Full fine-tuning costs much more. It can also overwrite what the model already does well (its learned priors). Our configuration trains approximately 9.3 million adapter parameters in total for both targeted DiTs. We use rank 8 adapters in the attention and feed-forward (MLP) layers of the sparse-structure flow DiT. We use rank 16 adapters in the attention layers of the shape flow DiT. The rank sets the size of the adapter matrices. A higher rank lets the adapter learn more.

A 3D model setup can need many dependencies and installation steps. We supply two Docker images (that you can run on Jobs or your own machine) with the necessary software. One image is for preprocessing, and one is for fine-tuning.

To train your LoRA adapters and upload them to the Hub:

Give the containers access to your data.

Set the parameters for your task.

Run the preprocessing container.

Run the fine-tuning container.

Then we explain the fine-tuning script, its settings, and how each setting affects training.

We’ll walk through three parts of the experiment:

Prepare the data. Convert GLB or OBJ meshes into the latent representations TRELLIS.2 uses for training, and render the input images.

Train the adapters. Run one job for each DiT, with the prepared dataset and a LoRA configuration.

Explain the code. Examine how the containers load the data, add adapters, and train the models.

We save the preprocessed dataset so that all training runs can reuse it.

items.body_ko:
요약: 이 블로그에서는 TRELLIS.2를 미세 조정하기 위한 스크립트와 컨테이너를 제공합니다. TRELLIS.2는 3D 자산에 대해 인기 있는 3D 모델이며 로컬 및 Hugging Face Jobs에서 실행할 수 있습니다. 미세 조정에 관심이 있다면 몇 가지 인수를 사용하여 스크립트를 사용하거나 (데이터셋을 Hugging Face Hub에 업데이트했다고 가정) 이 저장소에서 직접 수정할 수 있습니다. 더 자세히 알고 싶다면 스크립트가 어떻게 작동하는지 살펴보겠습니다. 시작해봅시다!

3D 생성은 로봇 공학, 시뮬레이션, 미디어 및 엔터테인먼트 분야에서 다양한 용도로 사용됩니다. 이러한 분야에서는 생성된 객체가 엄격한 규칙을 따르도록 하고 모델 및 데이터 표현을 표준화하는 것이 어렵습니다. GLB 및 PLY와 같은 다양한 파일 형식과 신경 방사 필드(NeRFs) 및 3D 가우시안 스플래팅(3DGS)과 같은 다양한 표현 방식이 있습니다. 각각은 다른 장단점을 가지고 있습니다.

TRELLIS는 통합 잠재 표현이라는 공통 내부 표현을 도입했습니다. 그 디코더는 이 표현을 필요한 출력 형식의 3D 모델로 변환합니다. 따라서 각 표현 형식에 대해 다른 모델을 사용할 필요가 없습니다.

동일한 팀은 TRELLIS.2를 출시했으며, 이는 3D 구조의 모델 표현을 개선합니다. 그러나 두 모델 모두 특정 작업에 모델을 쉽게 적용할 수 있는 방법을 제공하지 않습니다.

TRELLIS.2와 같은 범용 모델은 특정 응용 프로그램에 중요한 세부 사항에서 오류를 발생시킬 수 있습니다. 예를 들어, 사용자는 가구 모델에 대한 정확한 기하학적 형태가 필요할 수 있습니다. 해당 작업에 대한 미세 조정 없이 사전 훈련된 모델은 충분히 정확하지 않은 기하학적 형태를 생성할 수 있습니다. 우리는 실험을 위해 188개의 신발류 객체를 포함하는 GSO의 하위 집합을 사용합니다. 초기 테스트에서 사전 훈련된 모델은 일반적으로 올바르게 보이는 신발을 생성했지만 밑창이 정확하지 않았습니다. 우리는 LoRA가 밑창을 더 정확하게 만들 수 있는지 테스트합니다.

우리의 목표는 Google Scanned Objects (GSO) 데이터셋을 사용하여 특정 객체 범주에서 TRELLIS.2의 성능을 향상시키는 것입니다. 우리는 어떤 파이프라인 구성 요소를 미세 조정하고 어떤 구성 요소를 훈련 중에 변경하지 않고 유지할지 설명할 것입니다. 파이프라인은 구조, 상세 기하학적 형태 및 재료를 분리합니다. 따라서 우리는 우리 작업에 중요한 구성 요소만 미세 조정할 것입니다.

무엇을 고정할지 선택하는 것은 무엇을 미세 조정할지 선택하는 것만큼 중요합니다.

LoRA는 저랭크 적응(low-rank adaptation)의 줄임말로, 작은 어댑터 행렬을 훈련하는 동안 원래 가중치를 고정한 채로 모델을 미세 조정합니다. 이는 훈련 가능한 매개변수 수와 그라디언트 및 옵티마이저 상태에 필요한 메모리를 줄입니다. 우리는 Hugging Face의 PEFT 라이브러리를 사용하여 이러한 어댑터를 추가하고 훈련합니다. 더 자세한 정보는 우리의 LoRA 가이드를 참조하십시오.

Hugging Face Jobs는 클라우드 하드웨어에서 컨테이너화된 워크로드를 실행합니다. 우리는 전처리 및 훈련에 사용합니다. 대신 자신의 GPU를 사용하려면 아래의 로컬 Docker 명령을 참조하십시오. 시작하기 전에 다음 사항을 확인하십시오:

여기에서 얻을 수 있는 HF_TOKEN

DINOv3가 게이트 모델이므로 Hugging Face 계정은 DINOv3에 액세스할 수 있어야 합니다

자신의 데이터셋을 사용하는 경우, 시작하기 전에 메시를 Hub에 업로드하십시오.

훈련하기 전에 TRELLIS.2가 3D 객체를 어떻게 생성하는지 그리고 LoRA 어댑터를 어디에 추가할지 살펴보겠습니다.

TRELLIS.2는 다섯 가지 주요 단계가 있습니다: 이미지 배경 제거, 이미지 인코딩, 거친 구조 예측, 상세 기하학적 형태 생성, 재료 생성. 그런 다음 파이프라인은 결과를 텍스처 메시로 내보냅니다.

먼저 BiRefNet은 입력 이미지에서 배경을 제거합니다. 그런 다음 DINOv3-L은 이미지를 특징 토큰으로 인코딩합니다. 생성 모델은 이 토큰을 사용하여 3D 객체를 안내합니다.

희소 구조 생성(Sparse Structure Flow)

희소 구조 흐름 DiT는 객체의 거친 형태를 예측합니다. 16³ × 8 크기의 작은 잠재 공간을 만드는 확산 트랜스포머(DiT)입니다. 그런 다음 VAE 디코더는 이 잠재 공간을 64 × 64 × 64 점유 그리드로 변경합니다. 그리드의 각 복셀은 해당 위치가 객체의 일부인지 여부를 보여줍니다. 복셀은 3차원 픽셀입니다. 우리는 이 모델에 LoRA 어댑터를 추가합니다. 왜냐하면 그 출력이 기하학적 형태 단계를 안내하기 때문입니다.

O-Voxel 및 구조화된 잠재 공간

O-Voxel은 TRELLIS.2의 3D 형식입니다. 희소 복셀 그리드입니다. 객체 표면의 복셀만 유지합니다. 각 복셀은 메시 정점과 같은 로컬 기하학적 형태와 재료 속성을 유지합니다. 형식이 작기 때문에 CPU는 메시를 몇 초 안에 O-Voxel로 변경합니다. GPU는 몇 초 안에 O-Voxel을 다시 메시로 변경합니다.

구조화된 희소 잠재 공간은 TRELLIS에서 나옵니다. 3D 데이터를 희소 텐서에 유지하여 계산을 더 빠르게 만듭니다. 모델은 그리드의 복셀 중 약 10%만 사용하므로 빈 복셀에 계산을 낭비하지 않습니다. 따라서 형상 흐름 DiT 및 텍스처 흐름 DiT는 희소 트랜스포머입니다. 희소 구조 흐름 DiT는 밀집 트랜스포머입니다.

기하학적 형태 생성(Shape Flow)

형상 흐름 DiT는 점유 그리드와 DINOv3 특징 토큰을 사용하여 잠재 공간을 만듭니다. 또 다른 VAE 디코더는 이 잠재 공간을 512 × 512 × 512 해상도의 O-Voxel 기하학적 형태로 변경합니다.

우리는 객체의 형태를 제어하기 때문에 이 단계의 DiT에 LoRA 어댑터를 추가합니다.

재료 생성 + 메시 생성

마지막 단계에서 텍스처 흐름 DiT는 형상 잠재 공간과 DINOv3 특징을 입력으로 사용합니다. 이는 기하학적 형태 표면의 재료와 텍스처를 정의합니다. 그런 다음 VAE 디코더는 잠재 공간을 각 복셀에 대한 기본 색상, 금속성, 거칠기 및 알파 값으로 변경합니다. 우리는 이 단계에 LoRA 어댑터를 추가하지 않습니다. 우리 데이터셋에는 확산 색상 맵이 있지만, 이 단계에서 훈련에 필요한 별도의 재료 맵이 부족합니다. 또한, 우리의 문제는 신발의 형태입니다. 기본 모델은 이미 좋은 색상과 텍스처를 만듭니다.

마지막으로, 파이프라인은 기하학적 형태와 재료 속성을 텍스처 메시로 결합하고 GLB 파일로 내보냅니다.

우리는 희소 구조 흐름 DiT와 형상 흐름 DiT에만 LoRA 어댑터를 추가합니다. 이 DiT는 객체의 형태와 기하학적 형태를 제어합니다. 우리는 텍스처 흐름 DiT를 고정하여 현재 기능을 유지합니다.

우리 데이터셋에는 확산 색상 맵이 포함되어 있습니다.

items.title: Chinese frontier AI models carry the fingerprint of export-controlled GPUs
items.body:
Our forensic analysis of publicly released AI models finds evidence that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group have gained access to NVIDIA’s Blackwell GPUs, despite restrictions on exporting these chips to China, and are using that hardware to create their AI models. Six models released by these companies since April 2026 contain numerical patterns matching Blackwell hardware, whereas earlier models from the same companies match NVIDIA’s older Hopper generation. The findings suggest that several leading Chinese AI developers have begun using Blackwell to train their newest models. U.S. officials and press reports had already alleged that DeepSeek and Moonshot AI were using Blackwell chips, without publishing technical evidence.

The evidence comes entirely from the models’ own published weights, rather than from leaks or insider accounts. We recover traces of the models’ initial values, and then search for the hardware configurations and initial configurations that reproduce them; for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi K3, we also confirmed the match on physical Blackwell chips. The fingerprint identifies how the weights were created and supports, without proving, the inference that Blackwell also performed the training. Specially configured AMD hardware, which is also restricted from export to China, is the only alternative we have identified; we have excluded it for DeepSeek-V4-Flash, and consider it very unlikely for the other five models. Notably, our findings provide technical evidence of access to advanced computing hardware, but do not establish where the chips were located, how access was obtained, or whether export controls were violated.

Table 1. Hardware fingerprints in successive models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group Link ↗

• Requires a U.S. license for export to China; none have been reported.

A Hopper fingerprint cannot distinguish an H800 from an H100 SXM or H200; the H800 identifications above are lab disclosures, not findings of this method.

Full list of models in Appendix 2 ↓

Six models from four Chinese labs read as Blackwell-trained. DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M3 match NVIDIA’s Blackwell-class B200 or B300 chips, which have 148 processor cores (called streaming multiprocessors, or SMs). DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1-Pro and Ling-3.1-flash match the GB200 or GB300 chips, also Blackwell-class, which have 152 processor cores. Kimi K3.1-Pro starts from the same seed as K3, and may be a checkpoint of K3 with further post-training.

Chinese labs started training on Blackwell relatively recently. DeepSeek’s models read as Hopper-trained through DeepSeek-V3 (released in December 2024), and as Blackwell from DeepSeek V4 (released in April 2026). Moonshot’s models read as Hopper through Kimi K2.5 (January 2026) and as Blackwell from K3 (July 2026). One Moonshot model sits in between: Kimi K2.7-Code, posted six weeks before K3, is built on the Hopper-era weights but contains a small part that matches the B200 or B300. MiniMax’s models read as Hopper through M2.7 (April 2026) and as Blackwell from M3 (June 2026). Ant Group’s Ling-3.0-flash (August 2026) reads as Hopper, while its Ling-3.1-flash (October 2026) reads as Blackwell. The Hopper readings do not identify a specific chip: H800s, H100 SXMs and H200s share the same fingerprint.

Not every Chinese AI lab has switched to Blackwell. The newest models we could read from Alibaba (Qwen), Zhipu (GLM), Tencent, Xiaomi and StepFun all read as Hopper-trained. Meituan says its LongCat-2.0 was trained entirely on “AI ASIC superpods,” and we found no NVIDIA fingerprint in the model weights it’s released.

The method gets known answers right. For 24 specific models, the developer has publicly said what hardware was used. In every case, our method agrees with the public announcement. NVIDIA’s own Nemotron-3 Ultra, whose technical report names the GB200 for one phase of its training, reads as 152 SMs, the same as Kimi K3.

The matches are far stronger than chance would explain. Even unrelated numbers can appear to match when enough combinations are tried. Across the roughly 6 trillion seed-and-layout combinations in our search, the strongest chance match would be expected to reach about 8 sigma—a measure of how far a result stands above ordinary random variation. The strongest evidence for each of the six models ranges from 49 to 1,385 sigma. Even the weakest individual test we report reaches 20 sigma.

The training runs were data-center scale. From each model’s size and the amount of data it was trained on, we estimate that each run needed on the order of 1,500 to 3,500 Blackwell GPUs for one and a half to three months, about 12,000 across the five (Table 2), assuming each model was trained on the hardware that initialized it. These estimates are rough, and the ranges around them are wide. At roughly $70,000 per GPU—the cost implied by a Wall Street Journal report that about 36,000 Blackwell chips being installed in Malaysia for ByteDance’s use would cost more than $2.5 billion—the largest of these clusters would cost about $200 million, and the five together more than half a billion dollars. These figures cover only the final training runs; the labs’ total spending on export-controlled GPUs is likely in the billions of dollars.

Table 2. Rough scale of each training run Link ↗

Training tokens divided by the tokens per second we assume a Blackwell GPU sustained on a model of that shape, over the run length the release timeline suggests: about 45 days for DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 70 for DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 80 for Kimi K3, 60 for MiniMax-M3 and 100 for Ling-3.1-flash.

We are not confident in these estimates. They rest on assumptions that the weights cannot confirm. The first is how efficiently each lab used its GPUs (often called MFU): we assume less than NVIDIA’s published benchmark rates, in line with other disclosed Blackwell training runs, and no lab has published its own figure. The second is how many tokens each model was trained on: DeepSeek’s counts are its own, and we take them on trust; the others are our estimates. The third is how long each run lasted, which no lab has stated. The fourth is that training stayed on the hardware that created the weights. The figures cover only the final training run of each model, not experiments, earlier runs or serving.

A model’s weights, also called parameters, are the billions of adjustable numbers that determine how it processes information and produces answers. Training repeatedly adjusts these numbers; but before training can begin, they need initial values. In the software examined here, those values come from a pseudorandom number generation (PRNG) algorithm called Philox: Philox produces seemingly random numbers in a deterministic way. The starting input for Philox is a number called the “seed.” Given the same seed and settings, Philox produces the same numbers every time. This lets engineers repeat an experiment from the same starting point.

To fill billions of weights quickly, PyTorch, the software framework used in the development of most major AI models, divides the work that Philox does among many parallel workers on the GPU, called threads. (It does this through cuRAND, NVIDIA’s library for random number generation.) Each thread generates its own sequence of numbers from the seed and fills a particular set of positions. The number of threads then determines how those positions are shared out. On the NVIDIA chips examined here, a sufficiently large initialization uses the maximum of 2,048 threads for each processing unit, called a streaming multiprocessor (SM). A chip with more SMs therefore assigns the same job to more workers, changing where their numbers go.

items.title: Show HN: Kapso – Iterative learning from enterprise data
items.body: Hey HN! We're Alireza and Majid building Leeroo (https://leeroo.com/). Previously we’ve built AI systems for products with millions of users, including at LinkedIn and Meta. We’re now focusing on building AI systems for enterprise data. Today, we're open-sourcing Kapso (https://github.com/Leeroo-AI/kapso), an engine that runs experiments, deploys the best solution, and learns from every run.The nature of data work is iterative: investigate, form hypotheses, experiment, and improve based on what you learn. This bottom-up process is the only way to deliver meaningful outcomes quickly in large, messy enterprise data environments. Consultants gathering context in meetings or teams defining a business ontology upfront to fit into the data has no chance of execution, in quarters and sometimes years. An AI-native system should automate this process, compounding learning to each new investigation and implementation.For instance, one of our enterprise projects was moving a company off its old data estate onto a lakehouse with more than 30 source-system families, thousands of tables and transformations, and hundreds of BI reports. No individual or AI agent knew how that data estate was connected and operated. The only way to learn it was to investigate the company's repos, dbt models, documentation, and data itself and propose hypotheses about the estate, run experiments, and learn from them, until we understand how each system behaves and under which conditions.The iterative work goes beyond understanding how data and systems fit together, and the business operations. Building useful software is iterative too. Whether you’re optimizing a warehouse, building a lakehouse pipeline or predicting churn, you need to run experiments and learn what works best in that environment. As you deliver more projects, that know-how compounds, similar in principle to RL. RAGing documentation has little value until it has been tried in a specific environment and the consequences are learned. As with human engineering work, experimentation and learning should happen in a sandbox.We built Kapso for this kind of work, you give it an objective and success criteria, and it works towards an optimum solution that can be deployed on your stack.You can view a video walkthrough here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W4FHlza1fRsHere’s how it works…Kapso has a bank of lessons that are induced or deduced from the past experiments, and each carries a credence score, conditions on where it applies, and the evidence behind it. For each new experiment, an ideation module proposes ideas considering the earlier lessons, re-ranks them by expected return against the budget each would use, and sends the top-ranked ones to the implementor. Because the bank keeps learning from the past experiments in that environment, the proposed ideas are better suited to it than generic hypotheses from an LLM or RAG. Also, results of each experiment are verified by a verifier module that no experiment can access and cheat. As we’ve found when building such systems, sometimes the success criteria and evaluation tests need to be evolved. The experimentation modules can propose updates to the metrics and criteria for the verifier to approve or reject.After each run, learn() updates the bank of lessons’ scores and boundaries using the evidence from that run. Changes to the bank can also be A/B tested by running otherwise identical builds with the previous and updated banks. The bank is built on git, so you can share your experience with others, list the banks available to you, and update them (`kapso experience share/list/update` in CLI). The system is model-agnostic and coding-agent-agnostic.kapso.deploy(solution, target_stack) follows the same workflow, runs a shorter experimentation loop to adapt the best solution to the target stack (e.g. Docker, Modal, BentoCloud, LangGraph). Every domain has a harness to start from, you can write your own domain harness with /kapso:harness in the plugin or through CLI (kapso harness new <name>), and compound over that by running experimentations.We ran it on some public benchmarks and live competitions, with the following results…- Predictive modelling on relational databases: first on RelBench, Kumo AI (now Nvidia) and Stanford's benchmark, ahead of the best tabular foundation model (https://star-project.stanford.edu/relbench/leaderboard/). This shows that keeping the learning in the harness-level can beat foundational table models. Updating a bank of lessons costs far less than retraining a tabular foundation model.- ML Engineering: First on OpenAI's MLE-bench at submission, still among the top open-source systems (https://github.com/openai/mle-bench/pull/107).- AI competitions: ahead of the best agent the ALE-Bench authors at Sakana AI reported, and running autonomously at the live International Olympiad in AI 2026, above all 471 human contestants and in the top three AI systems (https://ioai-official.org/ai-models-track/ioai%c2%b2-2026-re...).We have a public bank for ML and Data at Leeroopedia (https://leeroopedia.com/): around 100k pages extracted by experimenting on papers and repos, about 6M requests a month, about 28% from AI agents.If you are at a growing company with a complex data estate across multiple systems and functions, and your data and AI team is stretched, we would love to help!https://github.com/Leeroo-AI/kapso

items.title: Show HN: Cerulion – ROS 2-compatible robotics runtime with multi-process replay
items.body: Hey HN! I'm Lakshay. Raveen and I have built Cerulion, a ROS2-compatible robotics runtime written in Rust. We've worked hard on lowering IPC transport latencies without making the single process tradeoff or forcing POD message types. These fast multi-process graphs can then be resimmed deterministically, and existing ROS2 nodes/launch files can run unmodified alongside native Cerulion Rust/Python code. Installation and quickstart (with a one-shot prompt for your favorite coding agent) here at the repo README: https://github.com/cerulion-inc/cerulionI worked on off-road autonomy during my PhD at MIT, and we kept running into inter-process latency in ROS (2 lidars and 6 cameras). Loaned messages need POD types, which nukes standard, vendor-agnostic Image/PointCloud2. We ended up running some hot paths in a brittle single process, which made debugging a nightmare. I'm sure you've seen the heisenbugs ROS-based stacks can produce, with no way to easily reproduce the consumption order or interleaving of callbacks. Valuable data of runtime failures on the robot was hard to use effectively without deterministic reproducibility.This is what we fix. Cerulion bags record per-input reads and scheduler traces alongside message content in standard MCAPs. cerulion bag play --resim all --verify re-executes node code on the recorded schedule and compares each byte for exact matches or within defined tolerances. Exit 0 is a match, 1 shows the first topic/frame that diverges, 6 shows schedule divergence and --report gives an optional CI verdict. Eligible ROS2 processes can replay deterministically as well.Here's the data loop:1. Run: Dependency-ordered level-based DAG scheduler with periodic/data/sync triggers, I/O deadlines, backpressure, and automatic profiling for process partitioning. Each node by default free-runs in its own process while preserving deterministic replay. Live runs pause/resume, and UMWAIT/WFE parks idle consumers on CPUs that support it. Wall-clock reads and runtime thread spawns in user code rejected at compile time by macros.ROS 2 is supported with rmw_cerulion for Foxy, Humble, Jazzy and Lyrical, that lets you run ROS2 nodes/launch files unmodified in the same graph as native Cerulion nodes. LD_PRELOAD gives ROS2 code shared memory loans through std::vector/std::string. cerulion ros2 attach folds in already-running ROS2 robots, and cerulion ros2 run/launch lets you run existing ROS2 workspaces on Cerulion without any additional setup (with an optional automatic migrate suggested that rewrites C++ publish sites).2. Move: iceoryx2 shared memory with no serialization, no payload copy and no payload-sized allocation, including for variable-length messages like sensor_msgs/Image and PointCloud2. Round trip latency for a 1MiB sensor_msgs/Image between two processes is 4.08µs p50, with a tight tail of 7.38µs p99 (under 2x p50), with recording on. This is default Cerulion, against 10.95 ms for default ROS 2 Jazzy. Cerulion's p50 and p99 stay flat from 64B to 16 MiB.3. Capture: With this round-trip latency, there are no tradeoffs, not for process isolation and not for bagging. We can afford always-on or event-based logging. Flashback is our robot dashcam: keeps ~30s of all logs and message contents in memory and saves it automatically on process crashes, topic stalls or declared incidents/manual triggers.4. Reach: A free account lets you pair robots and desks, letting all your devices find each other with no config, IP addresses or discovery chatter. Pubsub is authenticated and on-demand, with signed grants that the robot verifies offline. We use Iroh to hole-punch or relay over WAN, and mDNS over LAN to transmit data using QUIC. Remote topics mirror into local shared memory, and each device has a single network gateway.5. Diagnose: cerulion doctor scans for compile/run-time issues (better than Windows Troubleshooter I promise) and suggests fixes. Hindsight is an early access MCP to let agents analyze your bags.To get started: go to the repo, install Cerulion with the curl one-liner, and paste the prompt in Claude Code/Codex: https://github.com/cerulion-inc/cerulion#quickstart-run-reco.... Or shift your own gears, it's all in the repo that you should star!The CLI needs a free account, which we use to make device pairing as easy as AirDrop USED to be ;) Everything runs on Linux (x86_64/ARM64), macOS and Android (JNI), with more platforms coming.We'd love to hear your feedback! If you run ROS 2 on a real robot, point this at your stack and tell us what breaks.Docs: https://docs.cerulion.comSite: https://cerulion.com

items.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
items.body:
Hydrogen brings cutting-edge intelligence to everyone.

SVP, Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect, Google

Today, we’re introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen, bringing cutting-edge intelligence to everyone — with speed and efficiency for everyday coding and agentic workflows.

While our frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, excel at deep, long-horizon reasoning on your hardest problems, Hydrogen is built for rapid execution across diverse agentic workflows. With Hydrogen, we’re also bringing Gemini 4 to everyone — for all tiers of Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app, Google Search, and paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity.

Hydrogen surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level (51 vs. 50, and reaching 54 at its highest xhigh thinking setting), while often completing tasks faster than models in its class. Gemini 4 Hydrogen is priced flat across its entire 1 million-token context window at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

Unlocking efficiencies in multi-model workloads

In real-world software development, while teams rely on frontier models like Carbon and Argon for deep architectural judgment when designing systems or untangling subtle bugs, they still need a fast, disciplined execution model for writing code, running tests, and verifying changes. Hydrogen is built to stand on its own as a model for everyday work — or to pair with Carbon and Argon as the high-efficiency execution engine in multi-model workflows.

To help make this multi-model collaboration automatic, we’re introducing Orchestrator in Google Antigravity. Rather than using a single model from start to finish, Orchestrator dynamically switches between models like Carbon and Hydrogen within the same session. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Orchestrator reached near-Carbon task success rates while, on average, consuming 24% less quota and completing 19% faster. For workflows that require parallel agents, Carbon can act as the coordinator while Hydrogen can power worker and verifier agents to build and test changes simultaneously across isolated workspaces — helping teams ship complex projects faster without driving up token costs.

Scaling developer and enterprise workflows

Beyond multi-model workflows, Hydrogen is a major standalone upgrade for teams migrating from Gemini 3.8 Flash. It delivers significant leaps in both speed and intelligence — finishing tasks 2.5 times faster at its high default setting while more than tripling Terminal-Bench 4.1 scores (57% vs. 18.2%), cutting fabricated claims by more than 5x, and adapting cleanly when a tool call fails or a search returns empty. It also matches or outperforms competing models in its class across core developer and enterprise workflows:

Iterative repository coding and debugging: Hydrogen handles issue resolution, debugging, rapid iteration, and codebase Q&A with focused, surgical edits — delivering cleaner, production-ready code without rewriting unrelated files. It outperforms similar-tier models on SWE-sweep where it has to discover and repair bugs without breaking existing code. To explore large repositories efficiently, the model excels at natively batching file-read and search calls in parallel rather than inspecting files one by one; in early testing across complex graphs, SQL, and data-heavy enterprise workflows, our partners have seen Hydrogen run 2x to 2.8x faster while reducing token usage by 12% to 23%, compared to 3.8 Flash.

Open-ended agentic execution: On multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and broad codebase navigation, Hydrogen ranks #5 on Agent Arena, arena.ai’s live benchmark. For deep domain reasoning and analysis, it leads its class on HLE-Diamond (58.8%), ranks #1 overall on Vals Tax Agent Bench (52.3%), ties for #1 on the Vals Legal Research Bench (55.8%), and leads its class on AutomationBench-AA.

Multimodal knowledge work: Hydrogen pairs native 1 million-token input with up to 1 million output tokens to synthesize dense PDFs, spreadsheets, charts, audio, and recorded video into polished, cited reports and structured deliverables. It outperforms other models on the new Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark (53.4%) for end-to-end agentic knowledge work over complex visual files, and on Agents’ Last Exam v1.1 (71.6%) for end-to-end professional workflows.

Web development: On tasks where speed matters to developers, like live UI prototyping, design-to-code iteration, and interactive app building, Hydrogen generates more functional, feature-complete layouts in fewer prompts.

Using Hydrogen for on-the-fly 3D coding, Geminisland lets anyone add to a shared voxel island from a single prompt to generate custom structures live on the map that players can walk around and explore in first person. Try the live app.

Paired with our new Gemini front end design skill in Google Antigravity, Hydrogen built an e-commerce storefront in one shot complete with a WebGL2 topographic shader, pinned four-stage scrollytelling, a thermal split-slider, a 3D wireframe spec card, and a live finish configurator. Try the live app and the Gemini front end design skill.

In Google Antigravity, Hydrogen turned Google Sheets into an animated pixel canvas by shrinking thousands of cells combining Python, native =LET(...) formulas, and conditional formatting to paint and animate full-motion scenes directly inside a live spreadsheet.

Starting from a YouTube keynote video and a design template in Google Antigravity, Hydrogen generated a multi-slide presentation directly in Google Slides, then ran an autonomous audit-and-fix loop to catch overlapping text and clean up every slide layout.

With Gemini in Google Sheets, Hydrogen can help teams rapidly turn financial data into interactive models that dynamically adjust based on various forecasting scenarios, generating outputs over 30% faster than previous models in Sheets canvas.

Adaptable speed and intelligence across four thinking levels

We built Gemini 4 Hydrogen for real-world usability. Hydrogen’s four thinking levels — low, medium, high (default), and a new xhigh tier — offer a wide range of options across quality, latency, and cost, scaling in a smooth, predictable progression so you only wait and pay for the reasoning depth a task requires. Across thinking levels, Hydrogen matches or outperforms some of the competing models in its class while often finishing tasks faster and using fewer output tokens.

Fast, everyday help in the Gemini app and Search

For consumers, Gemini 4 Hydrogen makes it easier to get things done, staying on track and following instructions more closely across multi-turn conversations.

In the Gemini app, Hydrogen makes your everyday assistant even more helpful — it’s better at following your guidance, calling the right tools, and getting you to a reliable output with less back-and-forth.

Ready-to-go writing, research, and everyday work: Hydrogen sticks closely to your tone, format, and specific rules, so email drafts, study guides, rewrites, and documents come back ready to use on the first try. When you are comparing products or synthesizing dense material, it pulls together clear tables and visual breakdowns without dropping key details.

Connects the dots and gets more tasks done: Hydrogen breaks down your goal step-by-step, pulling relevant context from your uploads, Google apps like Gmail and Google Drive, and Connected Apps like Airtable and Dropbox. When you start a task in Gemini, it also more frequently calls the right tools and skills for the job, helping save you time as you check things off your to-do list.

Hydrogen은 모든 사람에게 최첨단 인텔리전스를 제공합니다.

SVP, Google DeepMind 및 최고 AI 아키텍트, Google

귀하의 브라우저는 오디오 요소를 지원하지 않습니다.

오늘, 저희는 Gemini 4 Hydrogen을 선보이며, 일상적인 코딩과 에이전트 워크플로를 위한 속도와 효율성으로 모든 사람에게 최첨단 인텔리전스를 제공합니다.

저희의 최전선 모델인 Gemini 4 Carbon과 Gemini 4 Argon이 가장 어려운 문제에 대한 심층적이고 장기적인 추론에 탁월한 반면, Hydrogen은 다양한 에이전트 워크플로에서 빠른 실행을 위해 구축되었습니다. Hydrogen을 통해 저희는 또한 Google AI Studio의 모든 티어, Gemini API, 기업용 Gemini, Gemini 앱, Google Search, 그리고 Google Antigravity의 유료 Google AI Pro 및 Ultra 구독자에게 Gemini 4를 제공합니다.

Hydrogen은 기본 높은 사고 수준에서 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index에서 Argon을 능가하며(51 대 50, 최고 xhigh 사고 설정에서 54에 도달), 종종 동급 모델보다 작업을 더 빠르게 완료합니다. Gemini 4 Hydrogen은 전체 1백만 토큰 컨텍스트 창에서 입력 토큰 백만 개당 1.50달러, 출력 토큰 백만 개당 7.50달러로 균일하게 책정됩니다.

다중 모델 워크로드에서 효율성 잠금 해제

실제 소프트웨어 개발에서 팀은 시스템을 설계하거나 미묘한 버그를 해결할 때 Carbon 및 Argon과 같은 최전선 모델에 의존하여 심층적인 아키텍처 판단을 내리지만, 코드 작성, 테스트 실행 및 변경 사항 확인을 위한 빠르고 규율 있는 실행 모델도 여전히 필요합니다. Hydrogen은 일상적인 작업을 위한 독립형 모델로 구축되거나, 다중 모델 워크플로에서 고효율 실행 엔진으로 Carbon 및 Argon과 짝을 이룰 수 있습니다.

이러한 다중 모델 협업을 자동으로 돕기 위해 Google Antigravity에 Orchestrator를 도입합니다. 처음부터 끝까지 단일 모델을 사용하는 대신, Orchestrator는 동일한 세션 내에서 Carbon 및 Hydrogen과 같은 모델 간에 동적으로 전환합니다. Terminal-Bench 4.0에서 Orchestrator는 Carbon에 가까운 작업 성공률을 달성하면서도 평균적으로 24% 적은 할당량을 소비하고 19% 더 빠르게 완료했습니다. 병렬 에이전트가 필요한 워크플로의 경우, Carbon은 코디네이터 역할을 할 수 있고 Hydrogen은 작업자 및 검증자 에이전트를 구동하여 격리된 작업 공간에서 동시에 변경 사항을 구축하고 테스트할 수 있습니다. 이는 토큰 비용을 높이지 않고도 팀이 복잡한 프로젝트를 더 빠르게 출시하는 데 도움이 됩니다.

개발자 및 엔터프라이즈 워크플로 확장

다중 모델 워크플로 외에도 Hydrogen은 Gemini 3.8 Flash에서 마이그레이션하는 팀을 위한 주요 독립형 업그레이드입니다. 속도와 인텔리전스 모두에서 상당한 도약을 제공합니다. 높은 기본 설정에서 작업을 2.5배 더 빠르게 완료하고 Terminal-Bench 4.1 점수를 3배 이상 높이며(57% 대 18.2%), 허위 주장을 5배 이상 줄이고, 도구 호출이 실패하거나 검색이 빈 결과를 반환할 때 깔끔하게 적응합니다. 또한 핵심 개발자 및 엔터프라이즈 워크플로에서 동급 경쟁 모델과 일치하거나 능가합니다.

반복적인 저장소 코딩 및 디버깅: Hydrogen은 관련된 파일을 다시 작성하지 않고도 문제 해결, 디버깅, 빠른 반복 및 코드베이스 Q&A를 집중적이고 정밀한 편집으로 처리하여 더 깔끔하고 프로덕션 준비된 코드를 제공합니다. 기존 코드를 손상시키지 않고 버그를 발견하고 수정해야 하는 SWE-sweep에서 유사한 티어 모델을 능가합니다. 대규모 저장소를 효율적으로 탐색하기 위해 이 모델은 파일을 하나씩 검사하는 대신 파일 읽기 및 검색 호출을 병렬로 기본적으로 일괄 처리하는 데 탁월합니다. 복잡한 그래프, SQL 및 데이터 중심 엔터프라이즈 워크플로에 대한 초기 테스트에서 당사 파트너는 Hydrogen이 3.8 Flash에 비해 2배에서 2.8배 더 빠르게 실행되는 동시에 토큰 사용량을 12%에서 23% 줄이는 것을 확인했습니다.

개방형 에이전트 실행: 심층 연구, 데이터 분석 및 광범위한 코드베이스 탐색과 같은 다단계 작업에서 Hydrogen은 arena.ai의 실시간 벤치마크인 Agent Arena에서 5위를 차지합니다. 심층 도메인 추론 및 분석에서 HLE-Diamond(58.8%)에서 동급 최고를 기록하고, Vals Tax Agent Bench(52.3%)에서 전체 1위를 차지하며, Vals Legal Research Bench(55.8%)에서 공동 1위를 기록하고, AutomationBench-AA에서 동급 최고를 기록합니다.

다중 모드 지식 작업: Hydrogen은 기본 1백만 토큰 입력을 최대 1백만 출력 토큰과 결합하여 밀집된 PDF, 스프레드시트, 차트, 오디오 및 녹화된 비디오를 세련되고 인용된 보고서 및 구조화된 결과물로 종합합니다. 복잡한 시각 파일에 대한 종단 간 에이전트 지식 작업에 대한 새로운 Multimodal Knowledge Agent(MKA) 벤치마크(53.4%)와 종단 간 전문 워크플로에 대한 Agents’ Last Exam v1.1(71.6%)에서 다른 모델을 능가합니다.

웹 개발: 라이브 UI 프로토타이핑, 디자인-코드 반복 및 대화형 앱 구축과 같이 개발자에게 속도가 중요한 작업에서 Hydrogen은 더 적은 프롬프트로 더 기능적이고 기능이 완비된 레이아웃을 생성합니다.

즉석 3D 코딩에 Hydrogen을 사용하는 Geminisland는 누구나 단일 프롬프트에서 공유 복셀 섬에 추가하여 플레이어가 1인칭으로 걸어 다니고 탐험할 수 있는 사용자 지정 구조를 맵에 실시간으로 생성할 수 있습니다. 라이브 앱을 사용해보세요.

Google Antigravity의 새로운 Gemini 프론트엔드 디자인 스킬과 짝을 이룬 Hydrogen은 WebGL2 지형 셰이더, 고정된 4단계 스크롤텔링, 열 분할 슬라이더, 3D 와이어프레임 사양 카드 및 실시간 마감재 구성기를 포함한 전자 상거래 상점을 한 번에 구축했습니다. 라이브 앱과 Gemini 프론트엔드 디자인 스킬을 사용해보세요.

Google Antigravity에서 Hydrogen은 Google Sheets를 수천 개의 셀을 축소하고 Python, 기본 =LET(...) 수식 및 조건부 서식을 결합하여 라이브 스프레드시트 내에서 전체 모션 장면을 그리고 애니메이션화하는 애니메이션 픽셀 캔버스로 변환했습니다.

YouTube 기조연설 비디오와 Google Antigravity의 디자인 템플릿에서 시작하여 Hydrogen은 Google Slides에서 직접 여러 슬라이드 프레젠테이션을 생성한 다음 자율 감사-수정 루프를 실행하여 겹치는 텍스트를 포착하고 모든 슬라이드 레이아웃을 정리했습니다.

Google Sheets의 Gemini와 함께 Hydrogen은 팀이 재무 데이터를 다양한 예측 시나리오에 따라 동적으로 조정되는 대화형 모델로 신속하게 변환하여 o를 생성하는 데 도움을 줄 수 있습니다.

items.title: I'm making LLMs work on small and old devices
items.body:
Run the biggest language model you can on the smallest hardware you own.

TV boxes, old tablets, single-board computers and routers all have a CPU, some RAM and flash storage that sit idle most of the day. smolmaxxing finds the biggest model each of them can really run, then pushes it further with custom kernels, careful memory use and weights streamed from flash. Every number in this repo was measured on the device itself.

Both devices run 8B and 16B mixture-of-experts models on about 1 GB of RAM by keeping only part of each model in memory and reading the rest from flash as it's needed.

More devices (phones, single-board computers, routers) are coming. The techniques aren't tied to one box: the 1-bit kernel needs only basic NEON, and the flash streaming works on any Linux or Android device with more model than RAM.

All of it is a patch on llama.cpp. The main ideas:

Kernels built for the chip. A 1-bit lookup-table kernel, repacked 2-bit and ternary formats for the Cortex-A55, and versions of them for the A7, which has no dot-product instructions.

Less RAM per model. Most of a small model's vocabulary is rarely used, so we drop those output rows. On the TV, a "headless" mode also stops the launcher and Google services while a model runs.

Experts paged from flash. A mixture-of-experts model only uses a few experts per token. We keep the popular ones in RAM, read the others from flash on demand and prefetch the next layer's. This is how 8B and 16B models run on 1 GB.

Streaming for dense models bigger than RAM, at the flash's full speed.

docs/how-it-works.md has every technique with its measured gain.

The quickest start is a ready-made model file from Hugging Face. They need the patched llama.cpp: stock llama.cpp can't load them.

TV box or another ARMv8.2 Android device: docs/tv-box-setup.md

Jailbroken iPad on iOS 12: ipad-air/README.md

All model files and how to rebuild them: docs/models.md

MIT. The llama.cpp patches are derivatives of llama.cpp (MIT). Model weights keep their own licenses, and the evaluation texts are Wikipedia excerpts (CC BY-SA 4.0).

Built on llama.cpp and llama2.c. Models from Qwen, unsloth (GGUFs and importance matrices), PrismML (Bonsai), inclusionAI (Ling-mini-2.0), tablinum (Moon-Beam), bartowski and mradermacher (GGUFs), Google (Gemma) and stories260K. The iPad is jailbroken with Amethyst. The banner uses Archivo (SIL OFL) and is rendered by tools/banner/render.sh. The 🤏 logo is the pinching-hand emoji from Google's Noto Emoji (Apache 2.0).

items.title: Distributed Ray Tracer
items.body: Hey HN, I'm Julius, I'm a backend engineer at Hatchet and created this demo to show off some of Hatchet's new features, primarily durable streams and serverless endpoints. Those, however, are just background details that made this significantly easier to scale. By distributing the rendering across many different nodes, orchestrated using Hatchet, it makes it possible to render quite high fidelity scenes fairly quickly. All of this would be possible on a single machine, but would be much slower without dedicated hardware (RT cores, etc).The renderer itself is using well-known ray tracing techniques, with no special considerations there. The renderer is a slightly modified version of https://github.com/ekzhang/rpt, with additional support for SDF scripting using https://docs.rs/fidget/latest/fidget/. SDFs have been popular in the demoscene community, though perhaps not super well known outside of that, and are capable of creating some fantastic looking scenes: https://www.shadertoy.com/view/ld3Gz2. The coolest part here is using a DSL to represent the SDFs in a rendering pipeline, and using LLMs with a chat interface to create them.The source is available here: https://github.com/hatchet-dev/distributed-ray-tracer

items.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Orchestrator
items.body:
Today, we’re rolling out Gemini 4 Hydrogen inside Google Antigravity alongside a new model dropdown option called Orchestrator, which pairs Hydrogen with our strongest models for long-horizon tasks, including Gemini 4 Carbon, in an optimized balance of quality, efficiency, and latency.

Selecting Orchestrator (Carbon) from the model selector in Google Antigravity.

Put Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen to work with Orchestrator

Earlier this week, we introduced Gemini 4 Carbon alongside /swarm for tackling massive, multi-worktree engineering tasks with parallel agent teams. In just a couple of days, tens of thousands of swarms have been launched on Antigravity, pushing frontier intelligence on the hardest problems.

For everyday feature work and debugging inside a single session, running a frontier reasoning model with multiple parallel agents on every step of every routine task slows down your loop and burns frontier quota. A common industry approach is to use a static “model router” that guesses task difficulty from your first prompt and routes the entire task to the cheapest model that is good enough to complete the task. Unfortunately, these start breaking down as agents become longer running, requiring different levels of complexity at different stages, often discovered as the task evolves.

Orchestrator takes a dynamic, bidirectional approach between Carbon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen within the evolution of a single trajectory. For example, Carbon can start in a read-only phase to explore dependencies, resolve ambiguities, and build a concrete plan with explicit re-planning triggers. Hydrogen could then take over to write edits, update packages, and run tests. If Hydrogen hits friction, it would hand back to Carbon to inspect the state, repair the plan, and resume execution. This allows Orchestrator to reach near-Carbon task success while being faster and more quota-efficient. On Terminal-Bench 4.1, Orchestrator reached near-Carbon task success rates while, on average, consuming 24% less quota and completing 19% faster.

Explicit multi-model pipelines with the Antigravity SDK: When you want programmatic control over which model handles each role, you can wire Hydrogen and Carbon together directly with the Antigravity SDK. In the demo below, an open-source issue triage system built with the Antigravity SDK pairs multiple agents together. The Hydrogen agents handle triaging and coding to keep up with incoming issue volume, searching the codebase, asking clarifying questions, and fast UI iteration from PR comments while the Carbon agent is assigned to larger refactors, new features, and security checks.

Pairing Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Gemini 4 Carbon with the Antigravity SDK for automated open-source issue triage and code generation.

Fast, dependable execution with Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Hydrogen also works as a standalone model for everyday coding and agentic work, scoring 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (surpassing Argon’s 50, and reaching 54 at its highest setting) and 57% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 (more than tripiling 3.8 Flash’s 18.2%). When selecting Hydrogen directly, you can dial reasoning depth across four thinking levels, low, medium, high (default), and a new xhigh tier.

Using Gemini 4 Hydrogen in Google Antigravity to upgrade dependencies, refactor shared utilities, and generate accessible image alt text.

Gemini 4 Hydrogen brings cutting-edge intelligence for everyday coding and agentic workflows. When you want frontier planning paired with speed without managing model switches, Orchestrator puts both Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen behind one prompt. Starting today, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is rolling out across paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. Orchestrator is rolling out as Orchestrator (Carbon) and Orchestrator (Argon) for Google AI Ultra subscribers, and as Orchestrator (Argon) for paid Google AI Pro subscribers, with additional models and plans supported in the future. Enterprises can access both in Gemini for business.

Pick one. It helps us reach more people like you.
items.body_ko:
오늘부터 Google Antigravity에 Gemini 4 Hydrogen을 출시하고, Hydrogen을 Gemini 4 Carbon을 포함한 가장 강력한 모델과 페어링하여 품질, 효율성, 지연 시간의 최적화된 균형을 통해 장기적인 작업을 수행하는 새로운 모델 드롭다운 옵션인 Orchestrator를 공개합니다.

Google Antigravity에서 모델 선택기에서 Orchestrator (Carbon)을 선택하는 모습.

Orchestrator로 Gemini 4 Carbon 및 Gemini 4 Hydrogen을 활용하세요

이번 주 초에 우리는 대규모의 멀티 워크트리 엔지니어링 작업을 병렬 에이전트 팀으로 처리하기 위한 /swarm과 함께 Gemini 4 Carbon을 소개했습니다. 단 며칠 만에 수만 개의 스웜이 Antigravity에서 시작되어 가장 어려운 문제에 대한 최첨단 지능을 확장했습니다.

단일 세션 내에서 일상적인 기능 작업 및 디버깅을 위해 모든 루틴 작업의 모든 단계에서 여러 병렬 에이전트와 함께 최첨단 추론 모델을 실행하면 루프 속도가 느려지고 최첨단 할당량이 소모됩니다. 일반적인 산업 접근 방식은 첫 번째 프롬프트에서 작업 난이도를 추측하고 전체 작업을 작업을 완료하기에 충분히 저렴한 모델로 라우팅하는 정적 “모델 라우터”를 사용하는 것입니다. 불행히도 에이전트가 더 오래 실행되면서 다른 단계에서 다른 수준의 복잡성을 필요로 하고, 종종 작업이 진화하면서 발견되는 경우 이러한 방식은 무너지기 시작합니다.

Orchestrator는 단일 궤적의 진화 내에서 Carbon과 Gemini 4 Hydrogen 간의 동적이고 양방향적인 접근 방식을 취합니다. 예를 들어, Carbon은 종속성을 탐색하고, 모호성을 해결하고, 명시적인 재계획 트리거를 사용하여 구체적인 계획을 구축하기 위해 읽기 전용 단계에서 시작할 수 있습니다. 그런 다음 Hydrogen이 편집을 작성하고, 패키지를 업데이트하고, 테스트를 실행할 수 있습니다. Hydrogen이 마찰에 부딪히면 Carbon으로 다시 넘겨 상태를 검사하고, 계획을 수정하고, 실행을 재개합니다. 이를 통해 Orchestrator는 Carbon에 가까운 작업 성공률을 달성하면서도 더 빠르고 할당량 효율적입니다. Terminal-Bench 4.1에서 Orchestrator는 Carbon에 가까운 작업 성공률을 달성하면서 평균적으로 24% 적은 할당량을 소비하고 19% 더 빠르게 완료했습니다.

Antigravity SDK를 사용한 명시적 다중 모델 파이프라인: 각 역할이 어떤 모델로 처리될지 프로그래밍 방식으로 제어하려는 경우 Antigravity SDK를 사용하여 Hydrogen과 Carbon을 직접 연결할 수 있습니다. 아래 데모에서 Antigravity SDK로 구축된 오픈 소스 이슈 분류 시스템은 여러 에이전트를 함께 페어링합니다. Hydrogen 에이전트는 들어오는 이슈 볼륨을 따라잡기 위해 분류 및 코딩을 처리하고, 코드베이스를 검색하고, 명확한 질문을 하고, PR 댓글에서 빠른 UI 반복을 수행하는 반면, Carbon 에이전트는 더 큰 리팩터링, 새로운 기능 및 보안 검사에 할당됩니다.

자동화된 오픈 소스 이슈 분류 및 코드 생성을 위해 Antigravity SDK로 Gemini 4 Hydrogen과 Gemini 4 Carbon을 페어링하는 모습.

Gemini 4 Hydrogen을 통한 빠르고 안정적인 실행: Hydrogen은 일상적인 코딩 및 에이전트 작업을 위한 독립형 모델로도 작동하며, Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index에서 51점(Argon의 50점을 능가하며 최고 설정에서 54점에 도달)을 기록하고 Terminal-Bench 4.1에서 57%(3.8 Flash의 18.2%보다 세 배 이상)를 기록했습니다. Hydrogen을 직접 선택할 때, 저, 중, 고(기본), 새로운 xhigh 티어의 네 가지 사고 수준으로 추론 깊이를 조절할 수 있습니다.

Google Antigravity에서 Gemini 4 Hydrogen을 사용하여 종속성을 업그레이드하고, 공유 유틸리티를 리팩터링하고, 접근성 있는 이미지 alt 텍스트를 생성하는 모습.

Gemini 4 Hydrogen은 일상적인 코딩 및 에이전트 워크플로를 위한 최첨단 지능을 제공합니다. 모델 전환을 관리하지 않고도 최첨단 계획과 속도를 원할 때, Orchestrator는 Gemini 4 Carbon과 Gemini 4 Hydrogen을 하나의 프롬프트 뒤에 놓습니다. 오늘부터 Gemini 4 Hydrogen은 유료 Google AI Pro 및 Ultra 구독자에게 제공됩니다. Orchestrator는 Google AI Ultra 구독자에게 Orchestrator (Carbon) 및 Orchestrator (Argon)으로, 유료 Google AI Pro 구독자에게는 Orchestrator (Argon)으로 제공되며, 향후 추가 모델 및 요금제가 지원될 예정입니다. 기업은 Gemini for business에서 둘 다 이용할 수 있습니다.

하나를 선택하십시오. 여러분과 같은 더 많은 사람들에게 다가가는 데 도움이 됩니다.

Release: llm-gemini 0.37

Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen today - the lowest cost member of the Gemini 4 family.

It's actually not too far off the price of its much bigger siblings, Carbon and Argon. I'm finding Gemini 4's pricing really confusing. Here's the pricing scheme:

Carbon and Argon are the same price, and both are scheduled to double in price on December 1st. If they're the same price, why have two different models? Google says that Argon "delivers Gemini 4 intelligence with faster responses and lower token spend per turn compared to Gemini 4 Carbon" - so it may be priced the same, but it will use less tokens per task.

Hydrogen, supposedly the cheap model, is currently only a 25% discount on its more capable peers. The Hydrogen price will make more sense after December 1st, when it will represent a 75% discount. It's still considerably more expensive than Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna - they're both $0.10/$0.50, so Hydrogen is 15x that.

I had Hydrogen generate some pelicans. Here's a full comparison grid showing the pelicans for all three members of the Gemini 4 family at their three supported effort levels:

Considering how close they are in price, the difference in pelican quality for Hydrogen is quite stark.

Here's how Google describe Hydrogen's intended position in their mix of models:

In real-world software development, while teams rely on frontier models like Carbon and Argon for deep architectural judgment when designing systems or untangling subtle bugs, they still need a fast, disciplined execution model for writing code, running tests, and verifying changes. Hydrogen is built to stand on its own as a model for everyday work — or to pair with Carbon and Argon as the high-efficiency execution engine in multi-model workflows.

Most notably, Hydrogen is the new free tier model, and is the model that will power AI features in Google Search.

items.title: [AINews] D-Day (Decision Models Day)
items.body:
Today was the “System One day” of the second annual AIE CODE event, and somehow everything aligned:

Cloudflare’s Michelle Chen walked through their Clef and Clairic models

Richard covered Diogo’s triumphant return to AIE talking about the Jevolution with their most notable production customers since crossing $100M ARR

In a BIG surprise, Google beat Anthropic to launching a production decision model, with Sundar and Logan announcing Gemini Decision 1, a calibrated multimodal decision model capable of taking up to 1000 questions and costing $0.10 per million input with ~200ms e2e latency.

Benchmarks are good (usual caveat about benchmarks):

And you can hear all this and more on today’s System One track.

And support AINews by giving your agent SerpApi to read and crawl the web!

Sponsored by SerpApi

Give Your AI Agents the Full Page, Not Just the Link
Retrieve public web pages by URL as clean Markdown, structured JSON, or raw HTML with SerpApi’s Extract API. Extract a single page, map a site’s URLs, or run a bounded same-site crawl. Simply set engine=extract with a URL, and add output=md for Markdown. Pair it with 100+ SerpApi search APIs to go from query to page content with one provider.

Thanks to SerpApi for working with business@latent.space!

AI Twitter Recap

Google Launches Gemini Decision 1 for Single-Pass Classification

Gemini Decisions API: Google introduced a new API backed by Gemini Decision 1. The model handles closed-set decisions, so it scores choices in a single pass instead of generating text token by token (Sundar Pichai, Logan Kilpatrick, Google).
Specs: It supports yes/no, multiple-choice and rubric scoring, with up to 255 multiple-choice options. It accepts text, image, audio, video and PDF inputs, handles up to 1,000 questions per request, has 256K context, returns answers in 150–250 ms end to end, and attaches a confidence score to every answer (@_philschmid).

Pricing: $0.10 per 1M input tokens, with $0 billed for output. Google says that is about 5x cheaper than Flash-Lite (Sundar).

Origin: The project started as an internal Google DeepMind prototype. A small team shipped the model and API about six weeks later (@_philschmid).

Google's comparison with TypeSafe's Jev: Google's own tests show Decision 1 beating Jev 1.14 on 5 of 7 shared benchmarks, including 92.2% vs 90.0% on JevBench. Jev costs $0.042 per 1M input tokens (@kimmonismus).

Artificial Analysis evaluation: Independent results are more mixed (Artificial Analysis).
Overall score: Decision 1 scores 66 on the Decision Index. That ties Elephant 9B and Jev 1.14, and sits 7 points behind Drex Max v1.1 and GLiDE v1.2.

Strengths and weaknesses: It leads AA-Omniscience-Decision (66) and HLE-MultiChoice (49). On AA-Paperclip, it answers every question correctly on only 33% of documents, versus 63% for Drex Max.

Cost and latency: It costs $345 per 1M tasks, versus $103 for Drex Max and $156 for Jev. Its Brier score is 0.18. Average time per task is 211 ms, slower than Jev at 92 ms (latency).

Early adopters: Stitch built a rapid-design experiment on the API that goes from a rough prompt to a multi-screen product flow in about 5 seconds (Stitch). LangChain shipped day-zero support with a base class shared with TypeSafe classifiers (LangChain).

Architecture pattern: At AI Engineer, Cloudflare described a hybrid agent design. Fast decision models handle tool selection and log extraction, and a large reasoning model handles diagnosis only. In its demo, this cut six LLM calls to one and about 40K tokens to 1.8K (TheTuringPost).

Frontier Model Evals: Fable 5.2 Leads, Carbon Draws Speed Complaints

Claude Fable 5.2 on Agent Arena: Fable 5.2 (Max) ranks #1 with a +30.4% net improvement across 4.7K real agentic sessions. That is about 1.6x the score of #2, Opus 5.5 (+19.5%). It is also #1 in Code, Work and Chat (Arena, Pareto view).
Pricing: API prices drop from $10/$50 to $8/$40 per 1M input/output tokens. Median cost per task is $7.3, versus $5.5 for Opus 5.5, $1.5 for Gemini 4 Carbon (High) and $6.0 for GPT-6-Astra.

Other evals:
AA-Robotics v0.1: Fable 5.2 leads at 75, ahead of Astra (69) and Sol (65) (AA).

VIALS-AA (visual reasoning): It scores 67% with tools but only 44% without them. Haiku 5.5 with tools reaches 49% at $0.07 per task (AA).

Debate benchmark: It won 209 of 224 debates in a Cambridge Union-style contest (@SamuelFitouss10).

Effort calibration: Within the Claude lineup, Artificial Analysis finds that moving up a model tier beats raising effort: Opus 5.5 at xhigh outscores Sonnet 5.5 at max with 40% lower cost per task (AA). Vals separately reports that Fable's "high" setting is often cheaper and better than xhigh or max (@RayanKrishnan).

Gemini 4 Carbon: Vals ranks Carbon #3 on its index, and the fastest and cheapest of the top five (Vals). Practitioner opinions conflict (Theo, Martin Casado, @MParakhin).
Latency complaints: Theo measured Carbon at low effort taking 22m21s, versus 9m33s for Opus 5.5 at high (timing). He also reports about 11 seconds to first token, roughly 20x Fable's, and attributes the delay to the server side (TTFT).

Coding and math: Casado calls Carbon "really good at code." Parakhin says Carbon often beats Fable on math and ML problems but that he does not trust it with coding.

Muse Ember: Meta's model posts +1.7% on Agent Arena at about $0.02 per task. That is roughly 4x cheaper than GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5, and about 12x faster than Luna (Arena). Vals reports Ember reaches 85% of Fable 5.2's performance at 0.84% of the cost (Vals).

Chinese models:
Qwen 4: Qwen-4-Max appears to be live. Rumors that it is disappointing remain unconfirmed (@kimmonismus). Some users are skeptical about how Alibaba has labeled its variants (@teortaxesTex).

ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview: Baidu's model is trending toward #2 among open models on Code Arena WebDev at 1668. Apache 2.0 weights are promised (Arena).

Nex-N2.6: This open multimodal agent model claims 83.0 on OSWorld and 84.1 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (Nex).

AI for Science, Verification and Robotics

Formal verification of Signal: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code framework produced Lean proofs of key security properties for unmodified libsignal, down to compiled machine code. Gemini agents generated over 6M lines of proofs, leaving humans to review the critical 1% (GDM, details).
Effort: A five-person team finished in four weeks. Verifying the seL4 microkernel took twenty person-years. When two old bugs were reintroduced, the system proved the buggy versions insecure (@omarsar0).

AlphaGenome 2: DeepMind's genomics model now conditions its variant-effect predictions on cell type and state. It can adapt to unseen states from a few dozen cells without retraining (@pushmeet, GDM thread).
Results: On TenK10K, it identifies 30% of causal variants versus 16% for the original model, and 43% of directional gene effects versus 23%. It also recovered the known ETS2 variant behind inflammatory bowel disease in gut macrophages.

Availability: It is available through the API for non-commercial research (Demis Hassabis).

Praxis-1 (Runway): Runway released a 27B MoE diffusion-transformer world action model with Apache 2.0 weights. It ranks #1 on RoboLab-120 (@jongranskog, @c_valenzuelab).
Claimed results: Runway says it finished tasks 15.6x faster than GPT-6 Astra driving the same arm, at 51x lower cost per task (Runway).

Ecosystem: vLLM-Omni has day-0 support (vLLM), and NVIDIA published NVFP4 checkpoints and a Jetson path (NVIDIA Robotics).

Gemini Robotics 2.5: The VLA model was evaluated on 200 tasks. Google reports 30–100% higher success rates and 20–30% faster completion than prior baselines. Gemini 4 Argon served as a simulation engine during development, and the model is rolling out to partners (Google, details).

Other robotics work:
GR00T 2: It ran a real-time, uncut chemistry experiment on dexterous hands (@DrJimFan).

RoboCap-10k: An open egocentric dataset of 10K hours with metric hand and h

AI 트위터 요약

Google, 단일 패스 분류를 위한 Gemini Decision 1 출시

Gemini Decisions API: Google은 Gemini Decision 1을 기반으로 하는 새로운 API를 도입했습니다. 이 모델은 닫힌 집합 의사결정을 처리하므로, 토큰별로 텍스트를 생성하는 대신 단일 패스로 선택 항목에 점수를 매깁니다 (Sundar Pichai, Logan Kilpatrick, Google).
사양: 예/아니오, 객관식 및 루브릭 채점을 지원하며, 최대 255개의 객관식 옵션을 제공합니다. 텍스트, 이미지, 오디오, 비디오 및 PDF 입력을 받아들이고, 요청당 최대 1,000개의 질문을 처리하며, 256K 컨텍스트를 가지며, 150-250ms의 엔드 투 엔드 시간으로 답변을 반환하고, 모든 답변에 신뢰도 점수를 첨부합니다 (@_philschmid).

가격: 100만 입력 토큰당 0.10달러이며, 출력에는 요금이 청구되지 않습니다. Google은 Flash-Lite보다 약 5배 저렴하다고 말합니다 (Sundar).

기원: 이 프로젝트는 Google DeepMind의 내부 프로토타입으로 시작되었습니다. 소규모 팀이 약 6주 후에 모델과 API를 출시했습니다 (@_philschmid).

Google의 TypeSafe Jev와의 비교: Google 자체 테스트에 따르면 Decision 1은 7개의 공유 벤치마크 중 5개에서 Jev 1.14를 능가하며, JevBench에서는 92.2% 대 90.0%를 기록했습니다. Jev는 100만 입력 토큰당 0.042달러의 비용이 듭니다 (@kimmonismus).

Artificial Analysis 평가: 독립적인 결과는 더 엇갈립니다 (Artificial Analysis).
전체 점수: Decision 1은 Decision Index에서 66점을 받았습니다. 이는 Elephant 9B 및 Jev 1.14와 동점이며, Drex Max v1.1 및 GLiDE v1.2보다 7점 뒤쳐집니다.

강점 및 약점: AA-Omniscience-Decision (66) 및 HLE-MultiChoice (49)에서 선두를 달립니다. AA-Paperclip에서는 33%의 문서에서 모든 질문에 정확하게 답변하는 반면, Drex Max는 63%입니다.

비용 및 지연 시간: 100만 작업당 345달러가 소요되며, Drex Max는 103달러, Jev는 156달러입니다. Brier 점수는 0.18입니다. 작업당 평균 시간은 211ms로, 92ms인 Jev보다 느립니다 (latency).

초기 채택자: Stitch는 API를 기반으로 한 신속 설계 실험을 구축하여 대략적인 프롬프트에서 다중 화면 제품 흐름을 약 5초 만에 생성합니다 (Stitch). LangChain은 TypeSafe 분류기와 공유되는 기본 클래스를 통해 day-zero 지원을 제공했습니다 (LangChain).

아키텍처 패턴: AI Engineer에서 Cloudflare는 하이브리드 에이전트 설계를 설명했습니다. 빠른 의사결정 모델은 도구 선택 및 로그 추출을 처리하고, 대규모 추론 모델은 진단만 처리합니다. 데모에서 이것은 6개의 LLM 호출을 1개로, 약 40K 토큰을 1.8K로 줄였습니다 (TheTuringPost).

프론티어 모델 평가: Fable 5.2가 선두, Carbon은 속도 불만 야기

Agent Arena의 Claude Fable 5.2: Fable 5.2 (Max)는 4.7K의 실제 에이전트 세션에서 +30.4%의 순 개선율로 1위를 차지했습니다. 이는 2위인 Opus 5.5 (+19.5%) 점수의 약 1.6배입니다. 또한 Code, Work 및 Chat에서도 1위입니다 (Arena, Pareto view).
가격: API 가격은 100만 입력/출력 토큰당 10달러/50달러에서 8달러/40달러로 인하되었습니다. 작업당 중간 비용은 7.3달러이며, Opus 5.5는 5.5달러, Gemini 4 Carbon (High)은 1.5달러, GPT-6-Astra는 6.0달러입니다.

기타 평가:
AA-Robotics v0.1: Fable 5.2가 75점으로 선두를 달리며, Astra (69)와 Sol (65)보다 앞섭니다 (AA).
